def countGoodPartitions(nums):
    MOD = 10**9 + 7
    n = len(nums)
    
    if n == 0:
        return 1
    
    first_pos = {}
    last_pos = {}
    
    for i, x in enumerate(nums):
        if x not in first_pos:
            first_pos[x] = i
        last_pos[x] = i
    
    # Count how many boundaries can be safely cut without splitting any repeated number
    # A boundary between index i and i+1 is valid if no number spans across it
    # Number k spans a boundary between i and i+1 if first_pos[k] <= i < last_pos[k]
    
    valid_boundaries = 0
    
    for i in range(n - 1):
        # Check if any number spans across this boundary
        is_valid = True
        
        # Check all numbers that span across this boundary boundary:
        # - first_pos[x] <= i and last_pos[x] > i
        # to efficiently check, we can filter based on the first_pos
        
        for x in first_pos:
            if first_pos[x] <= i < last_pos[x]:
                is_valid = False
                break
        
        if is_valid:
            valid_boundaries += 1
    
    return pow(2, valid_boundaries, MOD)
